display.purpose: Page heroes only. One per page.

label.purpose: Tracked uppercase eyebrow above headlines, sienna fill, paired with ◆.

micro.purpose: Form labels, fine print, hint copy.

mono.purpose: Credentials, IDs, dispatch sheet numerics, dollar figures.

shadows.name: shadow-sm
shadows.purpose: Default card resting shadow. Faintly grounded in paper.

shadows.name: shadow-md
shadows.purpose: Subtle hover lift. Primary CTA hover.

shadows.name: focus-ring

motion.name: transition-normal

narrative.overview: Y7's site reads like a specialized industry publication, not a marketing landing page. The visual language borrows from print trade journals: warm newsprint-cream paper stock, pressroom-ink type, a single burnt-sienna seal as the only accent, kicker eyebrows in tracked caps, restrained scale-and-weight hierarchy. The page earns the visitor's attention through substance, the way a quality trade publication earns readership: by speaking as an informed insider to other insiders, with operational language matched by operational typography. Recognition first, persuasion second, decoration never. The system explicitly rejects four aesthetic lanes named in PRODUCT.md: generic auto-broker template, SaaS-cream marketing, logistics-corporate, and crypto/startup. The Trade Bulletin posture is the antithesis of all four: it doesn't perform credibility, it documents it.
keyCharacteristics: Warm newsprint-cream surface (#F7F5F0), never pure white. Paper stock, not screen.
Pressroom-ink type (#2C2C2A), never pure black. Ink on paper, not pixels on screen.
Single burnt-sienna accent (#993C1D) used as a seal, not a flood. Restrained color strategy: tinted neutrals + one accent ≤10% of any given screen.
Georgia serif for headlines and titles; system sans for body and UI; JetBrains Mono for credentials, IDs, and structured numerics.
Hierarchy through scale and weight contrast (≥1.25 ratio), not loudness. No exclamation marks, no urgency theater.
Multi-layer subtle shadows (four-stop scale) carrying ambient depth, never decorative drop shadows.
All four locales (EN, RU, UK, PL) at typographic parity. Translation quality is operational quality.

rules.name: The One Seal Rule
rules.body: Burnt Sienna covers ≤10% of any given screen. Its rarity is the point. The CTA Strip block is the deliberate exception (a full-bleed accent surface used at most once per page).

rules.name: The No-True-White Rule
rules.body: The marketing surface is never #FFFFFF. The page is always Newsprint Cream. Card White exists only on top of cream as elevation, never as a base.

rules.name: The No-True-Black Rule
rules.body: Type and dark surfaces are never #000. Pressroom Ink (#2C2C2A) is the warmest near-black we use.

rules.name: The Status-Only Color Rule
rules.body: Bonded Pine and Cite Red exist only to express system state (success / error / verified). Never decorative.

rules.name: The Kicker–Headline Pair Rule
rules.body: Section headers are always a Label kicker (uppercase, sienna, with ◆) directly above a serif Headline. The pair is the trade-publication signature.

rules.name: The No Decorative Type Rule
rules.body: Never gradient text. Never text shadows. Never letter-spaced display copy beyond minor tightening. Emphasis comes from weight (400 → 700) and scale (≥1.25 ratio between steps).

rules.name: The Em-Dash Substitution Rule
rules.body: No em dashes (—) and no -- in copy. Use commas, colons, semicolons, periods, or parentheses.

rules.name: The Multilingual Parity Rule
rules.body: Russian / Polish / Ukrainian copy uses the same hierarchy and tracking as the English original. No demoted treatment.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces sit flat at rest. Cards have shadow-sm (barely there). Shadows escalate only on state.

rules.name: The No Glassmorphism Rule
rules.body: No backdrop-filter: blur as decorative surface treatment. PRODUCT.md anti-reference #4.

rules.name: The 3px Lift Cap Rule
rules.body: Card hover translateY caps at -3px. The trade-publication register stays controlled.

dos: Do treat Newsprint Cream (#F7F5F0) as the page background everywhere on the marketing site.
Do use Burnt Sienna (#993C1D) as a seal: kicker fills, primary CTAs, focus glows, link underlines, hover borders. ≤10% of any screen.
Do pair every section title with a tracked-caps Label kicker, optionally prefixed by ◆.
Do lead with operational specifics on every audience surface: USDOT #4427359, MC #1741537, $75k BMC-84 surety bond. Render IDs in JetBrains Mono.
Do vary card grid layouts across long pages.
Do keep status colors (Bonded Pine, Cite Red) for system state only.
Do maintain typographic parity across EN, RU, UK, PL.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion on every animation.
Do keep input font-size at 16px on mobile to prevent iOS zoom-on-focus.
Do state Y7 as 'Licensed & Bonded FMCSA Broker', never 'Licensed & Insured'.
donts: Don't use pure white (#FFFFFF) as a page background.
Don't use pure black (#000) on text or surfaces.
Don't ship gradient text. PRODUCT.md anti-reference #4.
Don't ship glassmorphism or backdrop-filter: blur as decoration. PRODUCT.md anti-reference #4.
Don't add neon accents, Web3-flavored gradients, or 'AI-native dispatch' copy. PRODUCT.md anti-reference #4.
Don't ship blue/red/orange marketing gradients, 'GET INSTANT QUOTE!' hero treatments, urgency timers, fake counter widgets, or cherry-picked review carousels. PRODUCT.md anti-reference #1.
Don't ship navy + gold logistics-corporate palette or 'Your global logistics partner since 1985' energy. PRODUCT.md anti-reference #3.
Don't use side-stripe borders (border-left > 1px as a colored accent).
Don't stack identical 3-card grids more than once per page.
Don't use modals as a first thought.
Don't use em dashes (—) or -- in copy.
Don't exceed -3px translateY on card hover.
Don't use Burnt Sienna as a decorative wash, divider, or large fill outside the CTA Strip exception.
Don't treat RU/UK/PL copy as smaller, looser, or visually demoted.
